name_note: Phocaeicola was split off from Bacteroides, so many genomes still labelled Bacteroides in NCBI, such as B. vulgatus and B. dorei, fall in this GTDB genus.

sentences.text: Phocaeicola is a genus of gut bacteria whose member Phocaeicola vulgatus was originally classified as a Bacteroides species.
Its member Phocaeicola vulgatus is one of the most abundant and ubiquitous bacterial species of the human gut microbiota.
These bacteria degrade complex heteropolysaccharides to short-chain fatty acids that the host partly uses, and are involved in synthesising vitamins and other bioactive compounds.
Phocaeicola dorei and Phocaeicola vulgatus are closely related, easily confused species that are also reported as important members of the infant gut microbiome.
A genetically engineered Phocaeicola vulgatus strain carrying an oxalate degradation pathway has been tested as a live therapeutic candidate for hyperoxaluria.
